## Variables

A variable is the name of a data manipulated by R. 

```{r}
foo <- 2.5
```

Three parts:

1) `foo`: name of the variable
2) `<-`: assignment operator (on the left the variable name, on the right the 
  value). If you have bad taste, you can replace it by `=`
3) `2.5`: the value

```{python}
#| eval: false
#| include: false
foo = 2.5
```

Basic numerical operations.

```{r}
12 / 4
```

Everywhere I would use a value, I can use instead a variable if the value of
the variable is compatible with what is expected. 

```{r}
foo * 2
```

### Types

Values (and therefore variables) have types. A type specifies what values are
possible (like integers versus real numbers) and what operations can be computed
on the values.

- real numbers `2.5`, `-1.35e-3`
- integers `135L` (for 135)
- logical values `TRUE` and `FALSE`
- strings (small texts) `"bla bla bla bla"` (between single or double quotes)
- functions (to be covered later)

```{r}
135L / 2L
2.5 > -1.2
```

```{r}
1/0
1/(-0)
12/Inf
Inf > 1e250
Inf - Inf
```

```{r}
typeof(foo)
typeof(TRUE)
typeof(135L)
typeof(135)
typeof("a text")
typeof(typeof)
typeof(class)
```
